purpose: Extend difftastic acceptance beyond the single before.py/after.py fixture pair by running the pinned difft 0.71.0 ($HOME/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/bin/difft, guarded launcher for tools/difftastic-0.71.0/difft) over every file changed in a real multi-file commit range of this repository, per gap-triage.json git-github-automation gap 4 ('difftastic acceptance is a single fixture pair ... not an LLM invocation or general quality benchmark'). Range: native-agent-stack-token-practice-review commit 231077d095511391e7dd8a5ab25c451331332c5e (parent) to bdd04ca50eb781f8366c955f481479b7a7f57cbd (this worktree's HEAD, 'Re-record the 12 trading layer verdicts from layer-specific packets (#74)'), 20 files changed spanning .json, .md, .py and .html. old/<path> and new/<path> were extracted with `git show <rev>:<path>` and verified byte-identical to `git show` output before running difft (spot-checked on docs/grand-catalog-handbook.md).
preregistered: If difft --display=inline exits 0 and produces non-empty, non-fallback output (no 'failed to parse' / 'could not find a parser' / panic message) for all 20 changed-file pairs, that settles the gap's specific complaint (single-fixture-pair acceptance) by demonstrating difft parses and reports every changed file in a real, larger, heterogeneous (json/md/py/html) changed set, not just the synthetic before.py/after.py pair -- while still not being a matched comparison against a challenger structural-diff tool (no second tool is installed; that remains open per gap 7). If any file fails to parse, produces empty output despite a real byte-level diff, or crashes difft, that file is recorded as a failure and the gap stays open for that file type.

verdict_impact.explanation: FIX ROUND 2026-09-22 (was 'settles_gap: partially' / direction 'supports_incumbent'; corrected per reviewer finding, no re-run of difft, only re-analysis of the same retained output). Per this check's own preregistration ('if any file fails to parse ... that file is recorded as a failure and the gap stays open for that file type'), 5 of 20 real changed files -- the two large JSON catalogs, both Markdown docs, and the large HTML ecosystem page -- fell back to difftastic's plain-text diff rather than a structural parse. Those are exactly the dominant real content types in this repository's own diffs (catalogs/*.json, docs/*.md), so this run does not settle gap 4's 'single fixture pair is not representative' complaint; it demonstrates the opposite for this repo's primary file types while confirming structural parsing does work for Python and modestly-sized JSON (15/20 overall). This is a genuine negative data point about difftastic's practical coverage on this repository, not evidence supporting the incumbent pick, and it is not itself sufficient to flip the layer's keep_but_compare stance absent a challenger tool to compare against (gap 7 stays open).

limitations: Not a matched comparison against any challenger structural-diff tool (gap 7 remains open); this is a single-tool scale extension, exactly as the gap's blocker text anticipated.
'Parsed_ok'/'parsed_structurally' is a mechanical check of difftastic's own header line for a fallback marker, not a manual review of diff quality or correctness for every file.

docs/ecosystem/index.html is a large single-line minified file; difft's inline report for it is 26,015,185 bytes and is kept only in the scratch dir (not copied into the repository) per the >1MB raw-output rule; its sha256 is recorded above.

This range was chosen because it was the worktree's own HEAD commit and already had a real 20-file multi-type diff on hand; it was not selected by any criterion related to diff difficulty or edge cases.

5/20 files fell back to Text rather than a structural parse: 2 due to DFT_GRAPH_LIMIT (large JSON), 1 due to DFT_BYTE_LIMIT (large HTML), 2 because difft 0.71.0 has no Markdown grammar at all (size-independent). No larger byte/graph limit was probed, and no attempt was made to check whether a smaller Markdown or HTML file would parse structurally, since gap 4 asks about this repo's actual changed-file set as-is.
